ruleName: Ball Lifted or Moved by Player
title: Practice Swing Accidentally Moves Ball in the Fairway
question: Your ball is lying on the fairway. Before playing your shot, you take a practice swing and accidentally hit the ball, causing it to roll several yards. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: There is no penalty because it was only a practice swing. Play the ball from its new position.
Count it as your next stroke and play the ball from where it came to rest.
You receive a one-stroke penalty. Replace the ball on its original spot before playing.

explanation: A stroke only occurs when you make a forward movement of the club with the intention of striking the ball. Because this was a practice swing, you had no intention of hitting the ball, so no stroke has been made. However, by accidentally hitting the ball, you caused your ball at rest to move. In the general area, the penalty is one stroke, and you must replace the ball on its original spot before making your next stroke.

Show a golfer on a neat fairway who has just taken a practice swing and accidentally struck the ball. The golfer should look surprised or concerned. Make the original ball position obvious, for example with a slight grass depression or mark, and show the ball a few yards further away on the fairway. Include a visible golf bag in the background and the course scenery, but no text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.

sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Illustrate a practice swing causing an accidental movement of the ball in the fairway (general area), making it clear no stroke was intended.
